subject: Geo boundary snapshot and KMS routing query
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@medscope.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: MedScope Security Team <security@medscope.com>
Date: 2026-11-25 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: regional hosting snapshot + KMS routing details for onboarding

Hi Ben,

Hope you’re well — we’re moving forward with the pilot and need a short package to complete our internal SIG/CAIQ review and legal onboarding. Specifically can you provide the following for EU production: 

- A per-region snapshot that shows where customer data may be processed/stored (nodes/zones) — we need the minimal set of locations and any standby failover zones.
- A KMS routing map that indicates which keys are stored/managed in which jurisdiction and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.
- Confirmation of VPC/privatelink behaviour: which egress paths are used for telemetry/metrics, and whether any control-plane callbacks cross regions.
- Any runbook/excerpt describing how we failover between regions without crossing EU borders for persistent data (short bullet list is fine).

Target deadline: Friday COB (3 business days). If you can’t meet that exactly, a staged delivery (snapshot + KMS map today, runbook next) is OK.

Also include filenames for anything you attach. We’ll reference these in our SIG evidence pack.

Thanks,
Anita
Anita Shah
Security Operations Manager, MedScope
anita.shah@medscope.com

[attachment: none]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@medscope.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: regional hosting snapshot + KMS routing details for onboarding

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver a concise package that covers each bullet. Plan below: 

1) Zonal snapshot (nodes + standby): we’ll export a one-page PDF with the active EU zones and standby zones and call out any transient cache locations. File: residency-snapshot-20261125.pdf

2) KMS routing map: CSV mapping of logical key IDs to region and manager type (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed). File: zonal-kms-routing.csv

3) VPC/Privatelink behaviour: an architecture SVG plus a short note on telemetry egress (we use private peering for data path; metrics telemetry goes to an EU metrics endpoint and does not include raw request payloads). File: privatelink-architecture.svg

4) Failover runbook excerpt: short bullets in the PDF and a link to the longer runbook in our internal drive.

We’ll deliver the residency snapshot and KMS CSV within 2 hours, and follow up with the SVG + runbook link by EOD. If MedScope requires a fully redacted SOC 2 extract as part of the packet, I can include the report link (we’ll provide redacted control narratives).

Are there any constraints on including transient cache nodes (Redis-style caches) in the snapshot, or should we only show persistent-storage locations?

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

[attachment: zonal-kms-routing.csv (to follow), residency-snapshot-20261125.pdf (to follow)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25 16:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: regional hosting snapshot + KMS routing details for onboarding

Ben — quick note: include the per-region outbound IP ranges for the EU zones (customer asks for these when dialing up private firewall rules). Also add a one-line on key rotation policy (annual rotation + emergency rotation process). I’ll draft the firewall snippet to paste into the PDF.

Irene
Senior Cloud Security Engineer, Redwood

[internal-only]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@medscope.com>
Cc: MedScope Security Team <security@medscope.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: regional hosting snapshot + KMS routing details for onboarding

Anita — attached is the initial packet per our plan. Summary below and next steps.

Attachments delivered:
- residency-snapshot-20261125.pdf — lists active EU zones, standby zones, and a short excerpt of the failover bullets.
- zonal-kms-routing.csv — logical key IDs mapped to region and manager (customer-managed indicated where applicable).
- privatelink-architecture.svg — high-level diagram of VPC/privatelink peering and egress paths.

Key notes:
- Persistent data for EU tenants remains in EU zones (active + standby). Cache nodes are transient and indicated in the PDF as cached-only; they do not hold canonical customer storage.
- KMS: by default account keys are Redwood-managed and encrypted in EU KMS partitions. We support customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) per contract; when used, keys can be stored in customer KMS in EU.
- Telemetry/metrics: aggregated metrics are sent to an EU metrics endpoint and do not include request bodies. Control-plane callbacks (for health/alerts) stay in the EU region unless a specific cross-region integration is requested and approved.
- Outbound IP ranges included in the PDF (page 2) for firewall allowlist.

Follow-ups / links:
- HubSpot ticket: HS-7421 (we’ll append the packet)
- Longer runbook (internal link): https://drive.redwood.internal/s/privatelink-runbook
- SOC 2 extract: https://app.redwood.com/reports/soc2-2026 (redacted control narratives available on request)

If this looks good, I can prepare a signed evidence bundle for your SIG pack (zip) and add a short exec summary. Please let me know if MedScope needs keys stored in a customer-managed KMS only (we can mark those hosts accordingly).

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

[attachments: residency-snapshot-20261125.pdf, zonal-kms-routing.csv, privatelink-architecture.svg]
